cause: B1's server-owned default registry contains only OLS and Panel covariance targets, and C2 Recipe payloads publish an empty memory target list.

impact: A current approved memory cannot safely supply the explicit time-index semantics required for a Recipe Notebook proposal, and an Agent cannot discover which bounded targets exist.

cause: The frontend has a candidate-review component and review API, but NotebookRouteView neither fetches pending candidates nor passes review handlers to NotebookSurface; the control plane also exposes no candidate-list read endpoint.
impact: A real user can manage libraries in Settings but cannot review a candidate in the visible Notebook lifecycle, so B2 cannot honestly claim browser evidence for an approved-memory source created through the product UI.
lesson: A review component is not a product capability until the route obtains its server-owned queue and wires explicit user actions back to the review service; do not substitute fixture setup for that user workflow.

cause: An independent reviewer inspected the B2 registry, Recipe vocabulary, and boundary tests after the focused suite passed.
impact: No correctness, maintainability, or test-quality issue was found. The review specifically confirmed no frequency inference and preserved explicit-value precedence.
lesson: When a memory may affect a model proposal, review must confirm both the exact writable path and the information it never reads; absence of frequency inference is as material as field-level allowlisting.

The existing C2 browser gate separately records fresh ETS and ARMA/GARCH Notebook-to-Draft-to-result lifecycles for this project. lesson: A time-series memory default may interpret an already selected time index, but it must never infer frequency or select a model; browser evidence must distinguish default visibility from statistical validity.
